title: 🌐 Where's your website?
excerpt: How to have a proper small web website within minutes; free, lightweight, easy.
content_html:
How to have a proper small web website within minutes; free, lightweight, easy.

“Oh I use Instagram.”

There's so many people I've come across whose thoughts and creations I would consume with pleasure. Yet most of them don't have their own blog/website and instead resort to the infinite scrolling slot machines whose plentiful issues and scandals require a distinct essay; 🔜. Aside from all that, these sites are ugly, slow, soulless, and force readers to sign up. No thanks.

Unrealistically but ideally one buys a domain name, codes their own site, and uses Codeberg and/or statichost to host it so that one ensures full control and safety of their content, e.g., easy migration if need be—this is what I do. However, considering how lazy/complacent/inept corporate social media has made the populace, or how scarce spare time is while working full-time, or the frequency of poorly written documentation, then not making one's own website is understandable. Below, three solutions. None of them Wix, Medium, nor Substack.

Read on if one wishes to trade in their excuses for a small web website that would run on a potato.‍[⇣] A cozy cobweb that reflects your personality.

Free hosting options

With the small web in mind I found these options, sorted according to a fickle preference:

  1. Mataroa.blog
  2. Pagecord.com
  3. Bearblog.dev

I'm a bit disappointed because without hesitation I would use all of them had I not become accustomed to having full control of aesthetics and functionality of my own website. However, a simple place to write is fine for most. Below are the links to my quick example homepages with the same content, and some first impressions. They all support Markdown syntax; to the non-geeks, this simply means it's easy to create titles, embed images, create bold fonts, et cetera.

🥇 Mataroa

“Naked blogging platform, for minimalists. Just write.”
  • Cost: free & $9/year
  • Features: https://mataroa.blog > features
  • Example homepage: https://arscynic.mataroa.blog

+ Mataroa gets my preference because it natively supports comments, and while free, the price for premium is commendably hard to beat.

- Annoying is that posts appear on the homepage by default, with large margins, which cannot be disabled.

🥈 Pagecord

“No lock-in, no AI,* no bloat. Just your words, written your way, on your own corner of the web.”
  • Cost: free & $39/year
  • Features: https://pagecord.com/#features
  • Example homepage: https://arscynic.pagecord.com

+ On Pagecord one can natively click embedded images to enlarge them. Another difference is that it's the only one that renders YouTube videos.

± It's the most feature rich option, but also the least straightforward and slowest of the three.† My gripe is that Pagecord's text editor immediately converts Markdown syntax into its graphical representation within the text editor, which I find intolerable, but I'm sure others would prefer.

– – –

* “[…] The “no AI” means no AI features. […]” The developer uses Claude to speed up the grunt work. I reached out and there's zero malicious ambiguity present. Since LLM use can be a deciding factor and is quite a divisive topic, I thought I'd mention it.

† Not to be interpreted as not straightforward, nor slow.

🥉 Bear

“A privacy-first, no-nonsense, super-fast blogging platform. No trackers, no javascript, no stylesheets. Just your words.”
  • Cost: free & $49/year or $189 once
  • Features: https://docs.bearblog.dev
  • Example homepage: https://arscynic.bearblog.dev

+ Bear has the most straightforward user experience and its default homepage design pleases me on par and sometimes more than Pagecord's. A surprisingly cool feature is that one can easily use an emoji or image as a favicon, and it natively supports LaTeX—yay math!

An indirect feature disadvantage of Bear is that free accounts are hidden from search engines and its own discovery feed. The former I find weird as it limits the reach of the small web and Bear's own success. The developer's response after reaching out:

“Free blogs can be unhidden from the discovery feed and search engines, they just need to go through a manual review process (https://docs.bearblog.dev/not-seeing-your-post/). This is because 30% of all new blogs are spam, and it turns out that upgrading is a good filter, as is opting in for a review.”

Verdict

One can't go wrong with any of them. The medals above can be dismissed as ornamental.

Embedding images

While uploading images to the above websites is supported, understandably unlimited uploads being a premium feature—software is not free, consider paying—I do suggest using a dedicated image hosting platform to simply embed its pictures instead. Why? It takes a load of their back and chiropractors make for bad dentists.

PixelUnion.eu is what I use, pay for, and strongly recommend. It uses Immich, which supports non-destructive image cropping! Moreover, PixelUnion is free below 15㎇ of storage.

How to embed an image hosted on PixelUnion?
  1. Create a public album, surf to its shared link yourself, left click on an image to open it, and now right click the image to select `Copy Image Link`. The link/URL now copied should look like https://YOUR_USERNAME.pixelunion.eu/api/assets/11bf5d37-8c5f-4652-a521-8912d3048082/thumbnail?slug=YOUR_GALLERY_NAME&size=preview&c=msYJHIQrdmg%2BmXigaYp1kGoHqg%3D%3D&edited=true
  2. Use the following Markdown syntax in the blog text editor: ![image_description](the_URL_copied_above)

“Not worth sharing.”

Nonsense. For the umpteenth time—unless posting food pics, then stay at Instagram—let this exquisite simulation of fireflies change your perspective: https://ncase.me/fireflies.* Your ideas matter. Just make something!

– – –

* The ambient sound only works in Chromium-based browsers.

POSSE

As opposed to governments—seriously 🤦—it's reluctantly understandable that some social media has become indispensable to a fair amount of one-person projects to network and find an audience, but that doesn't mean having to hold oneself hostage to the greed-driven whims of big corporations.

Now, with your own website, one can “Publish (on your) Own Site, Syndicate Elsewhere”.‍[⇣] Create the original content on your own platform of choice and share that on all other social media. POSSE reduces risk, increases agency, stimulates creativity, and makes happy the increasing amount of people sick of parasitic billionaires and their brain rot platforms.

―Angelino Desmet; 31 July 2026.

Latest edit: 3 August 2026.
  1. 2026-08-02: 1. Adds Fireflies and ANOTHER IDEA. 2. Adds footnote † to Pagecord.
  2. 2026-08-03: 1. Adds an omitted options section. 2. Adds bus factor section.

⚜︎

Omitted options

  • Pika.page omitted because I consider a free account post limit of 50 too harsh; feels slightly coercive even though I'm sure it's not meant this way.
  • Pico.sh/prose seems awesome, but command line is too complicated for non-technical folk to start off with.

🚍 Bus factor

The bus factor is “the minimal number of engineers that have to be hit by a bus for a project to be stalled”‍[⇣]. It's 1 for all three and they address it here: Mataroa, Bear, and Pagecord via mail:

“Good question. Bus factor 1, but since it's open source I do plan to make it clearer how it would be maintained in the event of my untimely death. Good nudge for me on this one. Many major indie products are bus factor 1.”

I left this out of the main section because I think: (1) it doesn't matter that much to the non-technical audience—they all have the same factor anyway, (2) there's an export function to save content, (3) judging by how lightweight all of these sites are and (4) by the trustworthy impression of the devs after my reaching out, I consider it unlikely they wouldn't find worthy maintainers in posterity.

However, if something were to happen and a hosting site eventually goes offline, then one loses all interactions such as likes and comments. More importantly, unless one uses a custom domain name, then every link on the Web that points to one's blog will stop working, i.e., a 404 Not Found error.

Sources

  1. The earliest TinEye trace leads back to a Polish website maluetar.soup.io of a user named Maluetar, but the original page seems forever lost.
    • Vladimir Prelovac, Kagi.com: small web.
    • Antony Lawn, The Paper Pilot: small web.
    • Viktor Lofgren: About Marginalia Search.
  3. Indieweb.org: POSSE.
  4. ACM Digital Library: Bus factor in practice.

Comment

content_html_zh:
如何在几分钟内拥有一个合适的小型网站；免费、轻量、简单。

“哦，我用 Instagram。”

我遇到过很多人，我会很高兴地欣赏他们的思想和创作。 然而，他们中的大多数人没有自己的博客/网站，而是求助于无限滚动的老虎机，其中的大量问题和丑闻需要一篇独特的文章； 🔜。 除此之外，这些网站丑陋、缓慢、没有灵魂，并强迫读者注册。 不，谢谢。

不切实际但理想的是，人们购买一个域名，对自己的网站进行编码，并使用 Codeberg 和/或 statichost 来托管它，以便确保对其内容的完全控制和安全，例如，如果需要，可以轻松迁移 - 这就是我所做的。 然而，考虑到懒惰/自满/无能的企业社交媒体已经让大众变得多么普遍，或者全职工作时业余时间是多么稀缺，或者文档写得不好的频率，那么不制作自己的网站是可以理解的。 下面给出三种解决方案。 它们都不是 Wix、Medium 或 Substack。

如果有人想用借口换取一个可以在土豆上运行的小型网站，请继续阅读。‍[⇣] 一张反映您个性的舒适蜘蛛网。

免费托管选项

考虑到小型网络，我找到了这些选项，并根据变化无常的偏好进行了排序：

  1. Mataroa.blog
  2. Pagecord.com
  3. Bearblog.dev

我有点失望，因为如果我不习惯完全控制自己网站的美观和功能，我会毫不犹豫地使用所有这些。 然而，对于大多数人来说，一个简单的书写位置就足够了。 下面是我的快速示例主页的链接，其中包含相同的内容和一些第一印象。 它们都支持Markdown语法；对于非极客来说，这仅仅意味着创建标题、嵌入图像、创建粗体字体等等都很容易。

🥇经典

“赤裸裸的博客平台，适合极简主义者。 就写吧。”
  • 费用：免费且每年 9 美元
  • 功能：https://mataroa.blog > 功能
  • 示例主页：https://arscynic.mataroa.blog

+ Mataroa 得到了我的青睐，因为它本身就支持评论，而且虽然免费，但高级版的价格却是无与伦比的。

- 烦人的是，帖子默认出现在主页上，边距很大，无法禁用。

🥈 页面线

“没有锁定，没有人工智能，*没有膨胀。 只是您的文字，以您的方式写在您自己的网络角落。”
  • 费用：免费 & 39 美元/年
  • 功能：https://pagecord.com/#features
  • 示例主页：https://arscynic.pagecord.com

+ 在 Pagecord 上，人们可以直接单击嵌入的图像来放大它们。 另一个区别是它是唯一可以渲染 YouTube 视频的。

± 它是功能最丰富的选项，但也是三个选项中最不直接和最慢的。† 我的抱怨是 Pagecord 的文本编辑器会立即将 Markdown 语法转换为文本编辑器中的图形表示形式，我觉得这是无法忍受的，但我确信其他人会更喜欢。

– – –

* “[…] “无人工智能”意味着没有人工智能功能。 [...]”开发人员使用 Claude 来加速繁重的工作。 我伸出手，发现存在零恶意歧义。 由于法学硕士的使用可能是一个决定性因素，并且是一个颇有争议的话题，所以我想我应该提到它。

† 不应被解释为不直接或缓慢。

🥉 Bear

“一个隐私第一、严肃、超快的博客平台。 没有跟踪器，没有 JavaScript，没有样式表。 只是你的话。”
  • 费用：免费，每年 49 美元或一次 189 美元
  • 功能：https://docs.bearblog.dev
  • 示例主页：https://arscynic.bearblog.dev

+ Bear 拥有最直接的用户体验，其默认主页设计与 Pagecord 的主页设计不相上下，有时甚至更令我满意。 一个令人惊讶的酷功能是，人们可以轻松地使用表情符号或图像作为图标，并且它本身支持 LaTeX - 耶数学！

Bear 的一个间接功能缺点是免费帐户对搜索引擎及其自己的发现源隐藏。 前者我觉得很奇怪，因为它限制了小网络的范围和贝尔斯登自己的成功。 联系开发商后的回复：

“免费博客可以在发现源和搜索引擎中隐藏，它们只需要经过手动审核过程 (https://docs.bearblog.dev/not-seeing-your-post/)。这是因为所有新博客中有 30% 是垃圾邮件，事实证明，升级是一个很好的过滤器，选择加入审核也是如此。”

判决

其中任何一个都不会出错。 上述奖牌可以视为装饰性的。

嵌入图像

虽然支持将图像上传到上述网站，但可以理解的是，无限上传是一项高级功能（软件不是免费的，请考虑付费），我建议使用专用的图像托管平台来简单地嵌入其图片。 为什么？ 这需要他们的背部负担，而脊椎按摩师则成为糟糕的牙医。

PixelUnion.eu 是我使用、付费并强烈推荐的。 它使用Immich，支持无损图像裁剪！ 此外，PixelUnion 存储空间低于 15 ㎇ 是免费的。

废话。 无数次 - 除非发布食物照片，然后留在 Instagram - 让这个精致的萤火虫模拟改变你的观点：https://ncase.me/fireflies。* 你的想法很重要。 做点什么吧！

POSSE

与政府相反——说真的🤦——令人不情愿地理解的是，一些社交媒体已经成为相当多的个人项目中不可或缺的网络和寻找受众的工具，但这并不意味着必须将自己作为大公司贪婪驱动的突发奇想的人质。

现在，通过您自己的网站，您可以“在您自己的网站上发布，在其他地方联合发布”。‍[⇣] 在您自己选择的平台上创建原创内容，并在所有其他社交媒体上分享。 POSSE 降低了风险，增加了代理性，激发了创造力，并让越来越多厌倦了寄生亿万富翁及其脑腐平台的人们感到高兴。

省略的选项

  • Pika.page 被省略，因为我认为 50 个免费帐户的发帖限制太严格了；感觉有点强迫，尽管我确信这不是这个意思。
  • Pico.sh/prose 看起来很棒，但命令行对于非技术人员来说太复杂了，无法开始。

🚍 总线系数

公交车因素是“项目陷入停滞时被公交车撞到的最少工程师数量”‍[⇣]。 这三个都是 1，他们在这里解决：Mataroa、Bear 和 Pagecord 通过邮件：

“好问题。 总线因素 1，但由于它是开源的，我确实计划更清楚地说明在我英年早逝的情况下如何维护它。 这对我来说是一个很好的推动。 许多主要的独立产品都是总线因子 1。”

我将其排除在主要部分之外，因为我认为：（1）对于非技术受众来说并不重要——无论如何，他们都有相同的因素，（2）有一个保存内容的导出功能，（3）根据所有这些网站的轻量级来判断，（4）根据我接触后开发人员的可信印象，我认为他们不太可能在后代中找不到有价值的维护者。

然而，如果发生某些事情并且托管网站最终离线，那么人们就会失去所有互动，例如点赞和评论。 更重要的是，除非使用自定义域名，否则网络上指向某人博客的每个链接都将停止工作，即出现 404 Not Found 错误。
